item.title: A note on the intractability of enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression
item.description: arXiv:2611.14471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, given a Horn expression and a family of inclusion-wise maximal satisfiable subsets of its clauses, deciding whether there exists another maximal satisfiable subset is NP-complete. As a consequence, unless P=NP, there is no output-polynomial time algorithm enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Defrain, Corentin Jazeron, Kazuhisa Makino

item.title: Combinatorial optimization with bounded subdeterminants
item.description: arXiv:2611.13065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We take a first step toward a broader study of classical combinatorial optimization problems through the maximum subdeterminants of their standard integer programming formulations, yielding new positive results for several famous (NP-hard) problems. An integer matrix is totally $\Delta$-modular if every square submatrix has determinant of absolute value at most $\Delta$. For every fixed $\Delta$, it has been known that maximum clique, maximum stable set, and minimum vertex cover can be solved in polynomial time on instances for which the coefficient matrix of the natural formulation is totally $\Delta$-modular. We extend this list by showing that the same holds for many other problems, including the weighted versions of maximum cut, the traveling salesman problem, feedback vertex set, odd cycle transversal, dominating set, max 2-sat, induced matching, and cluster vertex deletion, as well as for $k$-colorability and graph isomorphism. Our proofs reveal several new ways in which bounded subdeterminants impose combinatorial structure: they bound the size or maximum degree of the input graph, bound packings of cycles and other obstructions, or yield decompositions into tractable graph classes such as forests, chordal graphs, graphs of bounded treewidth, and graphs of bounded linear mim-width.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Fiorini, J. Pascal Gollin, Tony Huynh, Simon Keil, O-joung Kwon, Sang-il Oum, Roohani Sharma, Stefan Weltge

item.title: An Improved $(1+2e)$-Approximation Algorithm for Metric Data Placement
item.description: arXiv:2611.13224v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the metric data placement problem with site-capacity constraints and fixed installation costs, aiming to minimize the total cost of placing data (resources) and accessing their nearest copies. We develop a deterministic polynomial-time approximation algorithm based on a natural linear programming relaxation of the problem. Starting from an optimal fractional solution, we construct multiscale metric-ball partitions independently for each resource and connect overlapping balls at consecutive levels to form a flow network. The resource layers are then coupled through shared site-capacity arcs, allowing us to obtain an integral placement by minimizing a surrogate cost over a single min-cost circulation. By optimizing the choice of ball radii, we establish an approximation factor of $1+2e\approx 6.44$. To our knowledge, this is the best approximation guarantee for the metric data placement problem since its introduction by Baev and Rajaraman in 2001.
item.dc:creator: S. Rasoul Etesami

item.title: Greedy+Singleton for knapsack-constrained monotone submodular maximization has approximation ratio exactly $\beta^\star \approx 0.42944$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Greedy+Singleton is the textbook heuristic for monotone submodular maximization under a knapsack constraint: it returns the better of the cost-benefit greedy set and the best single item. Its worst-case approximation ratio, known only to lie in $[0.427, 0.42945]$ (Feldman-Nutov-Shoham; Kulik-Schwartz-Shachnai), is exactly an explicit constant $\beta^\star\approx 0.42944$. In the extremal instances, many cheap "filler" items wear down the value of two large optimal items while greedy spends the budget, until neither fits. This picture gives a sharper factor-revealing relaxation; we bound it analytically near the extremal parameters, up to finitely many interval-arithmetic checks, and certify it elsewhere by an exact branch-and-bound. The matching bad instances are tie-free and checkable by hand. For the version that stops at the first item that does not fit, Wolsey's bound $1-e^{-\beta_W}\approx 0.35780$, where $e^{\beta_W}=2-\beta_W$, is tight; Wolsey stated this for his variant without giving the instances, and we give an explicit family with no ties that also covers comparison with the best feasible singleton. The CELF rule also has ratio exactly $\beta^\star$.
item.dc:creator: Kundan Baliga, Aiden Xie, Aditya Byju

item.title: Approximating graphic TSP by b-matchings
item.description: arXiv:2611.13585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for graphic TSP that returns a tour of length at most $\frac{89}{64}=\frac{7}{5}-\frac{3}{320}$ times the value of the subtour relaxation. This improves the long-standing ratio $\frac75$ of Seb\H{o} and Vygen and shows that the integrality gap of the subtour LP on graphic instances is at most $\frac{89}{64}\approx 1.3906$. We optimize a non-linear objective function over an odd-join polytope, which uses (i) a new removable system of edges, and (ii) reconnection of subtours if the graph is disconnected. This approach gives a $\frac{13}{10}$-approximation algorithm for $4$-regular $4$-vertex-connected graphs, improving the $\frac43$ of Newman, and a $\frac43$-approximation for $k$-vertex-connected graphs of maximum degree at most $k+1$, for every $k\ge 3$. For the general graphic TSP, we construct a feasible point in the odd-join polytope, using an optimal vertex from the Subtour linear programming relaxation of TSP, which helps us bound the approximation factor by 89/64.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gupta, Mehrdad Sohrabi, Levent Tun\c{c}el

item.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.
item.dc:creator: Vedat Levi Alev, Shravas Rao

item.title: Local Modifications of Nearest-Neighbor and Min-Plus Representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.13787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how changing a Boolean-valued function at $d$ inputs affects the size and precision of its exact representations. Starting from a representation of size $m$, we prove four bounds, two for nearest-neighbor (NN) representations and two for integer min-plus representations. (i) For NN representations on a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$, at most $m+2d$ anchors suffice. The coefficient $2$ is optimal: on a three-point domain, changing one value can increase the minimum number of anchors from one to three. (ii) For NN representations on the Boolean cube with rational anchors, let $R$ be the maximum original coordinate bit length, and let $\Delta$ be the maximum bit length of the least common denominator of any one original anchor's coordinates. We construct a representation with at most $m+3d$ anchors on a common dyadic grid and coordinate bit length $O(R+\Delta+\log(n+1))$. (iii) For integer min-plus representations on the Boolean cube, we give a construction that keeps the original $m$ forms and their labels and adds at most $d$ new forms. Its maximum weight is at most $W+2n$, where $W$ is the largest absolute original coefficient, including constant terms. (iv) For integer min-plus representations on a finite rational domain $X\subset\mathbb{Q}^n$, at most $m+2d$ forms suffice. Their maximum weight is polynomially bounded in $m,d,W,n,|X|$, the coordinate bound, and the common denominator of $X$. The coefficient $2$ is again optimal: on a three-point domain, changing one value can increase the minimum number of forms from one to three. These bounds imply stability under polynomially many changes on the cube for polynomial-size representations, including those with polynomially bounded NN coordinate bit length or min-plus weight.
item.dc:creator: Liliia Redina

item.title: Optimal radio labelings for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.13813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a simple graph $G$, let $d(u,v)$ denote the distance between two vertices $u$ and $v$ in $G$, and let $diam(G)$ denote the diameter of $G$. A radio labeling of $G$ is a mapping $f : V(G) \rightarrow \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$ such that $|f(u)-f(v)|\geq diam(G) + 1 - d(u,v)$ holds for every pair of distinct vertices $u, v \in G$. The span of $f$ is the difference between the largest and smallest integers assigned by $f$, and the radio number $rn(G)$ is the minimum span taking over all radio labelings of $G$. Let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices and let $H$ denote the Heawood graph (see Figure-1). In this paper we determine the radio number for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph, and characterize all optimal radio labelings of $P_n \Box H$. Moreover, we show that the radio number of $P_n \Box H$ exceed the lower bound given for $rn(G)$ in [6], where $G$ is any graph, and that this gap is arbitrarily large.
item.dc:creator: Payal Vasoya, Miral Doshi, Devsi Bantva

item.title: Feedback Vertex Set, Max Cut, and Edge Coloring on the Strong Product of a Graph and a Path
item.description: arXiv:2611.13917v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We examine the computational complexity of well-known problems on subgraphs of the strong product of two paths. Namely, for Max Cut we show NP-hardness on induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ answering a question by Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Huynh, Joret, Liu, and Wood (2021). For 3-Edge Coloring we show NP-hardness on subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ and that it is equivalent to 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs for induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$. It is a long standing open question whether 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs is NP-hard. As a second contribution, we consider graphs of the form $G \boxtimes P$ and show that Feedback Vertex Set on these graphs is FPT in the clique-width of $G$. Furthermore, we show that it can be solved in polynomial time if $G$ is chordal or co-comparable and that the computational complexity depends on the parity of $P$ if $G$ is bipartite. Namely, it is solvable in polynomial time if $P$ has an even number of vertices but is NP-complete otherwise. For Max Cut, we show that it can be solved in polynomial time if $G$ is bipartite.
item.dc:creator: Jan Diester, Kolja K\"uhn, Manuel Rapp, Samuel Schneider, Torsten Ueckerdt

item.title: You Can Have It All: Small sparse induced-universal graphs for minor-closed classes
item.description: arXiv:2611.14194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that, for every fixed proper minor-closed graph class $\mathcal{G}$ and every positive integer $n$, there exists a graph $U_n$ with $n^{1+o(1)}$ vertices and edges such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of $U_n$. This result generalizes and unifies the results of Dujmovi\'c et al. (J. ACM 2021) on induced-universal graphs and the results of Esperet, Joret, and Morin (J. London Math. Soc. 2023) on sparse induced-universal graphs from planar graphs to all proper minor-closed graph classes. It simultaneously improves the previous bounds for the number of vertices in induced-universal graphs (previously $O(n^2)$ obtained as a corollary of a result of DeVos et al. (J. Comb. Theory, Ser. {B} 2004) and a result of Gavoille and Labourel (ESA 2007)) and the number of edges in subgraph-universal graphs (previously $O(n^{3/2})$ by Babai et al. (Theory and Practice of Combinatorics 1982)).
item.dc:creator: Vida Dujmovi\'c, Cyril Gavoille, Gwena\"el Joret, Piotr Micek, Pat Morin, David R. Wood

item.title: Characterizing Fixed-Treewidth Planar Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14327v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give the first inductive characterization of planar graphs of treewidth $k$ for each $k \geq 3$. Our definition generalizes the well-known inductive definition of planar $3$-trees and the recent definition of so-called planar quasi-$4$-trees [F\"orster, 2024]. As a key step, which may be of independent interest, we show that every planar triangulation $G$ of treewidth $k$ admits a tree decomposition of width $k$ where each adhesion set induces a cycle in $G$. As an application of planar quasi-$4$-trees, we show that planar graphs of treewidth at most $4$ have vertex arboricity at most $2$. That is, the vertex-set of every planar graph of treewidth at most $4$ can be partitioned into two sets that each induce a forest.
item.dc:creator: Laura Merker, Samuel Schneider, Torsten Ueckerdt

item.title: Directed Singular-Value Sparsifiers with $O(n \log n/\epsilon^2)$ Arcs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14342v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given an unweighted directed graph, a sparsifier is a nonnegative reweighting of original arcs that preserves every in-degree and out-degree exactly. In this work, we study singular-value sparsifiers, which are generalizations of spectral sparsifiers. Singular-value sparsifiers find a number of applications in theoretical computer science, such as maintaining directed cuts and flows, speeding up directed Laplacian solvers, and sparsifying dense weight matrices in neural networks. Strong singular-value (SV) approximation supports sparse representations of directed random walks with guarantees that remain stable under products, and controls bilinear error in the left and right Schur-complement metrics. We prove that every unweighted directed graph on $n$ vertices admits an $\varepsilon$-SV sparsifier with $O(n\log(2n)/\varepsilon^2)$ arcs, improving the $O(n\log^5 n/\varepsilon^2)$ support bound of Lau, Wang, and Zhou. The sparsifier is a nonnegative reweighting of original arcs and preserves every in-degree and out-degree exactly. We also give a randomized construction with $\tilde{O}(m+n)$ real-arithmetic running time, where $m$ is the input support size, and the output has the same support bound and rational weights of polynomial bit length.
item.dc:creator: Emile Anand

item.title: Online Graph Coloring: Competitive Ratios Separating Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2611.14513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study online coloring, focusing on the competitive ratio. The best previously known results were (1) a lower bound of $\Omega(n / \log^2 n)$ for both deterministic and randomized algorithms by Halld\'{o}rsson and Szegedy (1994), (2) an upper bound of $O(n / \log n)$ for randomized algorithms by Halld\'{o}rsson (1997), and (3) an upper bound of $O(n / \log \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms by Kawarabayashi, Yoneda, and Yoneda (2025). In this paper, we improve these results as follows: 1. A new lower bound of $\Omega(n / \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms. 2. A new upper bound of $O(n (\log \log n)^2 / \log^2 n)$ for randomized algorithms. 3. A new upper bound of $O(n / (\log \log n)^{2-\varepsilon})$ for deterministic algorithms for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. For randomized algorithms, we nearly close the gap between the lower and upper bounds; the remaining gap is only $O((\log \log n)^2)$. We establish the asymptotic separation between randomized and deterministic online graph coloring. Against an oblivious adversary, a polynomial-time randomized algorithm achieves a competitive ratio asymptotically smaller than any deterministic algorithm can guarantee, even with unlimited computation.
item.dc:creator: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Hirotaka Yoneda, Masataka Yoneda

item.title: Scheduling on identical machines with conflicts to minimize the total completion time
item.description: arXiv:2507.01759v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of scheduling jobs on identical machines with conflict constraints, where certain jobs cannot be scheduled simultaneously on different machines. We focus on the case where conflicts can be represented by a simple undirected graph, and the objective is to minimize the total completion time. We establish that the problem is strongly NP-hard even on two machines with two distinct processing times. For unit-time jobs, we prove that the problem is polynomially solvable on two machines for any conflict graph, but becomes strongly NP-hard on three machines. We further identify polynomially solvable cases for specific classes of conflict graphs. For the general problem, we propose mathematical models, lower bounds, and a genetic algorithm. We evaluate their performance through computational experiments on a wide range of instances derived from well-known benchmark instances in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Nour ElHouda Tellache, Lydia Aoudia, Mourad Boudhar

item.title: Strong Conflict-Free Vertex-Connection via Twin Cover: Kernelization and Chromatic Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2605.13299v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A strong conflict-free vertex connection coloring of a graph is a graph coloring for which, for every two distinct vertices of the graph, there exists a shortest path between them in which some color in said coloring appears only once. The strong conflict-free vertex connection number, denoted by $\operatorname{svcfc}(G)$, is the number of colors in the strong conflict-free vertex connection coloring with the smallest amount of colors out of all such colorings of $G$. We study the problem of deciding whether this number is at most some threshold together with the parameter twin cover. Our first result is that when we have given $(G,k)$ in which $k$ is some target number of colors and given some twin cover $X$ of $G$ which is of size $t$, there is a polynomial time reduction to an equivalent instance which has at most $\max\{2,t+k2^t\}$ vertices. This result allows us to give a kernel for Strong CFVC Number which is parameterized by $\operatorname{tc}(G)+k$, which implies that Strong CFVC Number is FPT w.r.t. the twin-cover number of $G$ so long as $k$ is fixed. Our second result is that if $G$ is a connected graph for which there exists a twin cover of size $t$, then $\chi(G)\le \operatorname{svcfc}(G)\le \chi(G)+t$. Our last result is an an exact expression for the chromatic number of graphs whose twin cover number is bounded. Namely, we show that for every proper coloring $\varphi$ of $G[X]$, the minimum number of colors needed to extend $\varphi$ to all of $G$ is $K_\varphi=\max_{S\subseteq X}(|\varphi(S)|+m(S))$, and hence $\chi(G)=\min_{\varphi\text{ proper on }G[X]} K_\varphi$. Our results indicate that twin cover is a meaningful parameter in the context of strong conflict-free vertex-connection, and show that once we have a fixed twin cover, the only difficulty left is in some additive threshold above the chromatic number.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 32nd International Computing and Combinatorics Conference (COCOON 2026), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 16835, pp. 397-408, Springer (2027)
item.dc:creator: Samuel German

item.title: Temporal Cliques Admit Linear Spanners
item.description: arXiv:2606.05156v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A temporal graph is a graph in which every edge carries a non-empty set of time labels, and it is temporally connected if for every two vertices $u$ and $v$, there exists a $u$-$v$-path with non-decreasing time labels. A spanner is a subset of its edges preserving temporal connectivity. Unlike static graphs, temporally connected graphs need not admit sparse spanners; nonetheless, minimizing spanner size is a central and widely studied problem. A particularly intriguing question is whether temporal cliques admit spanners of linear size. Despite considerable effort over the past years, the best known upper bound remained $O(n \log n)$. We finally resolve this question, proving that every temporal clique on $n$ vertices admits a spanner of size $7n$. Moreover, such a spanner can be computed in polynomial time.
item.dc:creator: Julia Baligacs

item.title: Multiway Partition is FPT for Connectivity Functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.10380v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E$ be a set of $n$ elements, $f\colon2^E\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ be submodular, $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in E$ be distinct, and $k\in\mathbb N$. The Submodular Multiway Partition problem asks whether $E$ has a partition $(P_1,\ldots,P_r)$ with $t_i\in P_i$ for all $i$ and $\sum_i f(P_i)\le k$. We prove that this problem can be solved in $r^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$ time whenever $f$ is posimodular. This covers monotone submodular functions, matroid rank functions, and nonnegative combinations of monotone and symmetric submodular functions. When $f$ is a connectivity function, we remove the dependence on the number of terminals and obtain a $k^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$-time algorithm. The proof is entirely elementary, and is arguably the simplest proof that Edge Multiway Cut is fixed-parameter tractable. As a new consequence, our main result immediately implies that Hypergraph Multiway Partition is fixed-parameter tractable.
item.dc:creator: Tony Huynh, Eun Jung Kim, Sang-il Oum, Roohani Sharma, Marek Soko\l{}owski

item.title: Convex Minimization with Integer Minima in $\widetilde O(n^4)$ Time
item.description: arXiv:2304.03426v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a convex function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose set of minimizers is nonempty and closed, lies in a box of radius $R$ with $\log R\le\mathrm{poly}(n)$, and has integral extreme points, we give a randomized algorithm that finds an integral minimizer of $f$ with high probability using $O(n^2\log n+n\log R)$ calls to a separation oracle, $O(n+\log R/\log n)$ calls to an approximate shortest vector routine such as the LLL algorithm, and $O(n^4\log(nR)\log\log n)$ other arithmetic operations. The previous best polynomial time algorithm [Jiang, SODA 2021, JACM 2022] achieves $O(n(n\log\log n/\log n+\log R))$ oracle complexity, but its overall runtime is at least $\widetilde{\Omega}(n^8)$. We obtain our speedup by combining a variant of the volumetric center cutting plane method of [Vaidya, FOCS 1989], run on the hybrid barrier of [Lee, Sidford, Wong, FOCS 2015] with the fast implementation of [Jiang, Lee, Song, Wong, STOC 2020], and a variant of the LLL algorithm that reduces segments of consecutive basis vectors recursively. The method runs in blocks, so that shortest vectors are computed only $O(n+\log R/\log n)$ times, and each computation takes $O(n^3\log^3 n)$ arithmetic operations in exact arithmetic. For submodular function minimization, our result implies an algorithm using $O(n^3\log n)$ calls to an evaluation oracle and $O(n^4\log^3 n)$ arithmetic operations in total. Its oracle complexity is better than that of the algorithms of [Lee, Sidford, Wong, FOCS 2015] and [Dadush, V\'egh, Zambelli, SODA 2018, MOR 2021], which had the best running time before this work.
item.dc:creator: Haotian Jiang, Yin Tat Lee, Zhao Song, Lichen Zhang

item.title: Layer-Based Width for PAFP
item.description: arXiv:2605.12457v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Path Avoiding Forbidden Pairs problem (PAFP) asks whether, in a directed graph $G$ with two of its vertices labeled $s,t$ and a set $\mathcal F$ of forbidden vertex pairs, there is an $s$--$t$ path that contains at most one endpoint from each pair in $\mathcal F$. We initiate the study of PAFP through a layer-based width measure. We first look at the directed union digraph $G\cup\mathcal F$, which is obtained by adding one arc per forbidden pair to $G$, oriented according to a fixed reachability-compatible order. Let the BFS layer $L_d$ be the set of vertices at directed shortest-path distance $d$ from $s$, and define the BFS-width from $s$ as $\max_d |L_d|$. We show that if $G\cup\mathcal F$ has BFS-width $b$ from $s$, and $p$ is the maximum, over BFS-layer cuts, of the smaller of the numbers of distinct heads and distinct tails of backward arcs crossing the cut, then PAFP is FPT parameterized by $b+p$. Here a backward arc goes from a later BFS layer to an earlier one. In contrast, we show that bounded BFS-width alone does not suffice: PAFP remains $\mathsf{NP}$-complete when the union digraph has BFS-width 2. We also study layer-based width parameters on the input graph. We show that if the input DAG has BFS-width at most $2$ and only $k$ backward input arcs, then PAFP can be decided in $2^k |I|^{O(1)}$ time, with unrestricted forbidden pairs, and this result is tight. Moreover, we study exact-length layers in the input graph, where the $d$-th exact-length layer consists of the vertices reachable from $s$ by a directed path of length exactly $d$. We show that for DAGs of exact-length width at most $2$, PAFP is polynomial-time decidable by a $2$-SAT encoding of fixed-length paths. Unlike previously known polynomial-time regimes our 2 input -graph tractability results simultaneously allow unrestricted forbidden pairs and input graphs with exponentially many $s$--$t$ paths.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 37th International Workshop on Combinatorial Algorithms (IWOCA 2026), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 16587, pp. 311-326, Springer (2026)
item.dc:creator: Samuel German

item.title: Computing Lower Bounds on the Nonnegative Rank via Non-Convex Optimization Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2605.14058v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix $X$ is the smallest number of nonnegative rank-one factors that sum to $X$. Since computing the nonnegative rank is NP-hard, it is common to circumvent this issue by computing lower and upper bounds. In this paper, we propose non-convex formulations and practical implementations for four important lower bounds for the nonnegative rank, namely the fooling set bound (FSB), the rectangle covering bound (RCB), the hyperplane separation bound (HSB), and the self-scaled bound (SSB). In particular, to the best of our knowledge, our algorithm for computing the SSB is the first available in the literature. We compute the SSB for several matrices for which its value had not previously been reported. In some cases, the SSB provides the best known upper bound, while the other three bounds do not. Moreover, on canonical benchmarks, we show that our non-convex approaches are often competitive with existing methods. The paper also provides a consolidated reference for the current state of several classical lower bounds on a large number of benchmark matrices.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Baeckelant, Arnaud Vandaele, Nicolas Gillis

item.title: Maximum Probability of Independence in Transitive Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2605.23291v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid on a finite ground set $E$, and suppose that the automorphism group of $M$ acts transitively on $E$. We show the following: if $X_1,\ldots,X_K$ are sampled independently from a distribution $p$ on $E$, then the probability that the samples are distinct and that $\{X_1,\ldots,X_K\}$ is an independent set in $M$ is quasi-concave in $p$ and maximized when $p$ is uniform. For $2\le K\le\rank(M)$, we characterize all maximizers by uniform total mass on the parallel classes and, in particular, show that the maximizer is unique and has global quadratic stability when $M$ is simple. As a corollary, for a random $K\times N$ matrix over a finite field with i.i.d.\ rows, uniform sampling from the nonzero vectors maximizes the probability of full row rank. Finally, we show that uniform sampling maximizes $\Prob\big(\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)\ge r\big)$, and hence also $\E\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)$, for every $L, r$.
item.dc:creator: Mladen Kova\v{c}evi\'c

item.title: List coloring uncrowded hypergraphs at the shattering threshold
item.description: arXiv:2606.18048v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A foundational theorem of Ajtai, Koml\'os, Pintz, Spencer, and Szemer\'edi asserts that every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph (i.e., with girth at least $5$) of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ contains an independent set of size $cn(\log\Delta/\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. Improving an earlier bound of Frieze and Mubayi, Iliopoulos showed that every such hypergraph has list chromatic number at most $(1+o(1))(k-1)(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$. Determining the optimal leading constant in this bound remains a major open problem. A natural target, suggested by the coupon-collector heuristic, is $(k-1)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, which also corresponds to the shattering threshold for coloring sparse random hypergraphs. Our main result shows that this target is attained: for every integer $k\ge2$, every $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ satisfies: $$\chi_\ell(\mathcal{H})\le(1+o(1))\Big((k-1)\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}.$$ In particular, this confirms a 2019 conjecture of Molloy for uncrowded hypergraphs. Building on this result, we prove that every $k$-uniform linear hypergraph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ has chromatic number at most $(c_k+o(1))(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, where $c_k\to1$ as $k\to\infty$, thereby proving a conjecture of Verstra\"ete and Wilson on the independence number of linear hypergraphs in the stronger form of colorings. Our techniques also yield a palette sparsification theorem for uncrowded hypergraphs, partially answering a question of Casselgren and Eriksson.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku, Minh-Quan Vo

item.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.38386v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14,639,440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.
